ticket.title: ks1204 cells: three tampers stay green - the array-like allow-list, the refusal message class, and the connector info reader are unpinned (#1035 gate N-B, test-only)
ticket.description:
# KS-1237 X-MSG-MEMBER (+ the held Q-ARRAYLIKE cell, one hunk) - Wednesday's task for Ornith, VITEST, **TEST-ONLY MODE, MODIFY THE EXISTING TEST IN PLACE** (two hunks) (written 07:2x AEST on 2026-09-18)

Written from origin develop `34cdcfb26`. The test file
`Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/ks1204-a-non-array-allow-list-fails-closed-and-documenttype-wins.test.ts`
(292 lines, blob `f1f9840ed`) was read whole; `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts` was read at `:1226-:1229`.

**WHY BOTH CELLS ARE IN ONE HUNK.** The `KS-1204 N-2` describe has exactly ONE fence whose context lines are all non-blank and free of
backticks, `${}` interpolation and non-ASCII - the three lines 243/244/245 - and both rows have to land there. So they go in together.
The array-like cell was ALREADY red-proven in its own run against its own tamper (`READY_KS-1237-ARRAYLIKE_…`, PASS 7/7); this run
red-proves the MESSAGE cell against the message tamper, and the array-like cell rides along as a CONTROL that must stay green.

## THE MODE - read this twice

TEST-ONLY, MODIFY IN PLACE. This service runs **VITEST** (`vi`, not `jest`). Your diff contains EXACTLY ONE file - the test file
above - with `--- a/<path>` / `+++ b/<path>` and **TWO hunks**. **No hunk for `verification.ts`.** Do NOT create a new test file.
Do NOT copy the reference test - ignore it.

## What is wrong (one paragraph)

`POST /api/documents` refuses a configured allow-list that is not an array with a FIXED message naming the allow-list
(`verification.ts:1227`). The #1035 gate measured that **nothing pins that message**: its tamper X-MSG-MEMBER - the refusal instead
names the caller's own type - gives **0 reds**. On the tampered app a non-array connector is told it is *"not permitted to register
document type SSD_DOCUMENT"* for the very type its own list names, and *"undefined"* for an untyped body, so **a misconfiguration
becomes indistinguishable from an ordinary type refusal** and no cell notices. This task adds the cell that pins the exact message,
alongside the already-proven array-like cell.

## Where (no product site changes - this list is informational; every line below STAYS)

- `:1226` - (correct) `        if (rawAllowedTypes !== undefined && rawAllowedTypes !== null && !Array.isArray(rawAllowedTypes)) {` - the fail-closed guard. Stays.
- `:1227` - (correct) `          res.status(403).json({ success: false, error: { code: 'FORBIDDEN', message: 'Connector document-type allow-list is not a list; refusing until it is corrected' } });` - the refusal this task pins. The tamper replaces this line. The message string occurs ONCE in the file. Stays.

## The exact change - TWO hunks in the TEST file

**HUNK 1 - two new cells.** INSERT them immediately BEFORE the existing `control: an ARRAY allow-list` cell. **Your `+` lines come
FIRST and your three context lines come AFTER them** - file lines 243, 244, 245, none of them blank. **There is NO blank line anywhere in
your output** - not as a context line and not as a `+` line. Round 1 of this task failed for exactly that: it was asked for a trailing
empty `+` line, emitted 13 `+` lines instead of 14 while keeping the header that promised 14, and the hunk reanchored FOUR LINES LATE
(to 247), landing both cells INSIDE the `control: an ARRAY allow-list` cell and reddening it and COMPLETENESS.

```
+  it('RED KS-1237 MSG1 - a non-array allow-list refusal names the ALLOW-LIST, not the caller type', async () => {
+    RAN.add('non-array message class');
+    connectorAllowedTypes = 'SSD_DOCUMENT';
+    const { status, body } = await createDocumentWithBody(CONNECTOR, { documentType: 'SSD_DOCUMENT' });
+    expect([status, body?.error?.code, body?.error?.message]).toEqual([403, 'FORBIDDEN', 'Connector document-type allow-list is not a list; refusing until it is corrected']);
+  }); // KS-1237 MSG1
+  it('RED KS-1237 AL1 - an array-like allow-list is not a list: 403 FORBIDDEN for a named type and an untyped body', async () => {
+    RAN.add('non-array an array-like');
+    connectorAllowedTypes = { 0: 'SSD_DOCUMENT', length: 1 };
+    const named = await createDocumentWithBody(CONNECTOR, { documentType: 'DOCUMENT' });
+    const untyped = await createDocumentWithBody(CONNECTOR, {});
+    expect([named.status, named.body?.error?.code, untyped.status, untyped.body?.error?.code]).toEqual([403, 'FORBIDDEN', 403, 'FORBIDDEN']);
+  }); // KS-1237 AL1
   it('control: an ARRAY allow-list ["SSD_DOCUMENT"] admits SSD_DOCUMENT and refuses DOCUMENT, as before', async () => {
     RAN.add('array control');
     connectorAllowedTypes = ['SSD_DOCUMENT'];
```

**HUNK 2 - register BOTH cells in COMPLETENESS, or an EXISTING cell goes red.** `KS-1204 COMPLETENESS` asserts `[...RAN].sort()`
**equals an exact list**, so a cell that calls `RAN.add` without being listed turns that existing control RED. Change line 289 only:

```
     expect([...RAN].sort()).toEqual([
       'string vs DOCUMENT', 'non-array the string "SSD_DOCUMENT"', 'non-array an object', 'non-array an empty string',
-      'array control', 'unrestricted control', 'precedence admits documentType', 'precedence refuses documentType',
+      'array control', 'unrestricted control', 'precedence admits documentType', 'precedence refuses documentType', 'non-array an array-like', 'non-array message class',
     ].sort());
   });
```

The `+` lines are byte-exact - copy them, including the two trailing `// KS-1237 …` comments. Indentation: 2 spaces for each `it(`
and its closer, 4 spaces for the statements inside. The cells read only names declared ABOVE them (`RAN`, `connectorAllowedTypes`,
`createDocumentWithBody`, `CONNECTOR`); `it` and `expect` are vitest globals. Do NOT import anything.
The `+` lines contain no non-ASCII character, no backslash, no dollar sign, no backtick and no double quote **except** the two inside
the COMPLETENESS entry `'non-array the string "SSD_DOCUMENT"'`, which is an UNCHANGED context line, not yours to alter.

Red under the tamper: **MSG1** fails at `.toEqual` by assertion - the tampered line answers a different message, so MSG1 reads
`[403, 'FORBIDDEN', 'Connector is not permitted to register document type']`. Green at the tip: the message is the fixed allow-list
one. **AL1 is a CONTROL here and must stay GREEN on both trees** - it asserts only status and code, which the message tamper does not
move (it was red-proven separately against the array-like tamper). Every existing cell also stays green: the only cell that reads
`body?.error?.message` is the N-3 precedence refusal at `:281`, whose 403 comes from the allow-list MEMBERSHIP check, not from this
not-a-list guard, so the tampered line is never reached on that path.

## Red cells

- RED KS-1237 MSG1

## Tamper (test-only mode - the checker plants this in a clone of verification.ts to prove your new cell can go red)

line: 1227
from: `          res.status(403).json({ success: false, error: { code: 'FORBIDDEN', message: 'Connector document-type allow-list is not a list; refusing until it is corrected' } });`
to: `          res.status(403).json({ success: false, error: { code: 'FORBIDDEN', message: 'Connector is not permitted to register document type' } }); // TAMPER: KS-1237 red-proof, the refusal names a type instead of the allow-list (the #1035 gate row X-MSG-MEMBER)`
statement_ok: the `from` line is a COMPLETE statement - one `res.status(403).json({...});` call ending in `;` with balanced brackets - and it is the entire body of the guard opened at `:1226`, followed by `return;` at `:1228` and the block close at `:1229`. The tamper replaces the message STRING ONLY: same status, same error code, same shape, so nothing but a message assertion can see it.

## Output

Exactly ONE ```diff block containing ONLY the modified test file, then TWO hunks in file order:
`@@ -243,3 +243,16 @@` (**13** `+` lines, NONE of them empty, then context 243/244/245) and
`@@ -287,5 +287,5 @@` (context 287/288, one `-` line 289, one `+` line, context 290/291).

## Premises (measured)

- **P1 tip.** origin develop `34cdcfb2663b9e4c31025044e6f842ad2c5a10a3`; source checkout clean, read verbs only.
- **P2 the files at the tip.** ks1204 test blob `f1f9840ed`, 292 lines; the hunk-1 context (243/244/245) is byte-compared and the 3-line sequence occurs exactly ONCE, all three non-blank. The tamper `from` line is at `:1227` and its message string occurs **once** in `verification.ts`.
- **P3 the gap.** #1035 tier-1 gate, tamper table row **X-MSG-MEMBER**: 0 reds, with the consequence read from the report's own consequence section. Quoted, not re-measured.
- **P4 the COMPLETENESS trap, READ not assumed** (`:285-292`): `[...RAN].sort()` must EQUAL the list, hence hunk 2 carries BOTH new entries.
- **P5 why AL1 rides along:** N-2 has exactly one clean fence (243/244/245) and both rows need it, so they share a hunk. AL1 was red-proven in its own run against its own tamper (`READY_KS-1237-ARRAYLIKE_…`, PASS 7/7, A2 strict); here it is a control.
- **P6 this brief's hunks through the REAL checker**: **RESULT PASS (7/7)**, apply_mode=**strict**. A3c 14/14, A3d clean; **A4 under the message tamper 1 failed / 11 — the declared cell MSG1 only, by assertion**; every control green INCLUDING **AL1** (which is why it can ride along) and `KS-1204 COMPLETENESS`; A5 11/11; A6 api-gateway 565 -> 567, 0 new red; A7 tsc rc 0.
- **P6b a typed-header slip, caught by the assembler before any run.** This brief's Output line first said `@@ -243,3 +243,15 @@` with '12 `+` lines' while the computed hunk is **14** lines -> `+243,17`. Third instance of that family this week, and the same costume that broke KS-1229 r1 this morning: **the header is taken from the tool that computes it, never from my own count.**

## Notes for the raise (not for the model)

- **Behaviour change: none.** Test-only: two new cells and their COMPLETENESS registration.
- **Raise tier: TIER 2.** **Refs KS-1237, not Closes** - X-INFO-ALWAYS-EMPTY remains, and it needs a `GET /api/connector/info` call for which this file has NO helper today (measured: the only fetch helper posts to `/api/documents`).
- **On PASS this SUPERSEDES `READY_KS-1237-ARRAYLIKE_…`** - same hunk, one more cell. Supersede only on PASS; on FAIL the array-like READY still stands.
